svg.title: Order hooks in the order they fired when an order is created and moved to processing
svg.desc: A timeline observed with HPOS enabled and data sync off. wc_create_order and the first save fire woocommerce_before_order_object_save, then the placeholder post of type shop_order_placehold is inserted, which fires save_post_shop_order_placehold, save_post and wp_insert_post, then woocommerce_new_order and woocommerce_after_order_object_save. Later saves fire woocommerce_update_order. update_status to processing fires woocommerce_order_status_processing, then woocommerce_order_status_pending_to_processing, then woocommerce_order_status_changed. The book-era hooks save_post_shop_order, added_post_meta and updated_post_meta never fired, so code that relied on them no longer runs; the replacements are woocommerce_new_order, woocommerce_update_order and the order status hooks.
svg.text: What an order save fires under HPOS
wc_create_order(), add_product(), calculate_totals(), save(), update_status( 'processing' ) on WooCommerce 11.2.1, sync with posts off

g.text: 1 woocommerce_before_order_object_save (every save, 9 times in the run)
3 woocommerce_new_order (once, with the order ID and object)
The first two are the book-era way to react to an order
save; with HPOS the order is not a shop_order post and
its data is not post meta. payment_complete fires only when
a gateway calls payment_complete(), not on a manual change.
Then read and write through the WC_Order object:
The numbers 1 to 6 are the order in which each hook first fired. woocommerce_new_order fires after the row exists, not before.
woocommerce_update_order fires on every later save, including saves WooCommerce itself triggers, so keep its callbacks idempotent and cheap.
woocommerce_before_order_object_save lets you change the object before it is written, and
woocommerce_after_order_object_save runs after it has been written.
